title: Oliv AI product documentation
text: Oliv’s source-grounded V1 reference now connects agents and operational tasks with all 555 buyer criteria, 91 AI checks, seven revenue domains, ICP guidance and the complete 735-question research bank. Review evidence and unresolved claims before relying on a workflow.

title: Oliv AI product documentation · Review what is evidenced and what needs confirmation
text: Use the status buttons at the top to inspect the dated source assessment, then open a criterion’s detailed reference. “Source-backed” is distinct from a shipped feature or an approved public claim. The supplied buyer map has 305 Evidenced, 100 Partial, 146 Unknown, 3 historical No and 1 ambiguous By design row. All 555 owner-decision cells are unmarked.

title: Oliv AI product documentation · What Oliv does
text: Oliv works with an existing revenue stack. Conversations and business records become connected account and opportunity context; specialist agents use that context to prepare work, surface changes and carry out configured actions. Salesforce or HubSpot can remain the system of record. The current product presentation distinguishes three things: the context foundation, agents that perform specific jobs, and apps that organize team workflows. A team can begin with a defined use case rather than replacing its entire stack.

title: Oliv AI product documentation · Choose your starting point
text: Start with the job you want to complete. A seller preparing for a meeting needs different setup and evidence from a RevOps leader allowing CRM writes or a CS manager reviewing account health.

title: Oliv AI product documentation · Read this V1 correctly
text: This is a source-grounded review draft, not a certification that every described capability is available in every workspace. Current public product pages set the naming and presentation; accessible internal agent documents add detail; dated Help Center articles provide setup and support context. Each page separates documented behavior from unresolved rules. Source publication dates, HTTP retrieval dates and product release dates are different. A source-backed description does not establish a plan entitlement, enforced permission or guaranteed completion time.

title: Evidence and claims workbench · What the status buttons mean
text: Source-backed = described in the 9 October source assessment; Partial = incomplete evidence; Needs confirmation = no evidence established; Reported no = dated assessment of missing proof; By design = one ambiguous CRM prerequisite row. text: TR2, TR7 and TR9 are historical proof-visibility gaps. P2 has ambiguous criterion polarity and needs owner interpretation. Do not read these four rows as four missing product features.

title: Getting started
text: A successful first deployment has a clear owner, a defined input, an observable output and an agreed point where a human reviews the work.

title: Getting started · Start with one outcome
text: Choose a bounded workflow: prepare opportunity-linked meetings, propose CRM field updates, review pipeline risk or prepare account-health briefs. Establish which records and people are in scope and what success looks like before increasing volume.

title: Getting started · Recommended setup sequence
text: Confirm the app and agent entitlement for the selected users. Connect the calendar, CRM and conversation sources needed by that workflow. Provide the relevant qualification criteria, ownership rules and process exceptions. Agree review, approval and notification behavior with the implementation owner. Run a small set of representative cases, including an exception or failure, and check the resulting records.

title: Getting started · Check the deployment boundary
text: Setup instructions vary by connector and organization policy. Some public setup copy describes an assisted rollout rather than a fully self-service configuration. Obtain the current connector steps for your environment instead of assuming every named integration uses the same installation path.

title: Plan your first deployment
text: Use the first deployment to establish a dependable operating workflow, not just a visually complete demonstration.

title: Plan your first deployment · Define the implementation scope
text: Write down the job, the users, the records in scope, the expected outputs and the integrations that those outputs depend on. For a CRM update workflow, include the object and field categories; for a meeting workflow, include meeting ownership and recording method. The website offers customer-operated and Oliv-operated implementation paths. Confirm who maintains the process playbook, connector configuration, exception rules and ongoing improvements in the agreed engagement. Business owner Who accepts the output and owns the workflow Technical owner Who connects systems and resolves permission issues Scope Users, teams, accounts, opportunities and excluded records Action boundary Read, draft, write, send and human review points Evidence What proves a successful run and where it is recorded

title: Plan your first deployment · Prepare the inputs
text: Provide access to the CRM and the relevant calendars, recordings, email or collaboration sources. Identify the current revenue process and qualification framework. A process document should state actual decisions and exceptions, rather than a desired future process. Where the source is incomplete or contradictory, record the disagreement for the responsible owner. Do not fill the gap with an inferred discount rule, ownership policy or customer communication permission.

title: Plan your first deployment · Recommended acceptance checks
text: Use a representative record and verify the correct account, contact and opportunity associations. Check the proposed output against the source conversation and agreed process. Test a case that should require review and verify the actual approval destination. Confirm that a changed setting persists and that the correct user can change it. Disconnect or expire a test integration in a controlled environment and observe the user-visible failure. Record the entitlement, configuration and verified date with the accepted result.

title: Plan your first deployment · Timelines and dependencies
text: Public pages describe several setup timelines for different use cases. These are not a single service-level commitment. Connector approval, historical data access, custom process work and customer review can change the schedule. Use an agreed implementation plan with explicit milestones. This V1 does not promise a universal five-minute setup, same-week deployment or fixed time to value.

title: Connect your revenue stack
text: Connections serve different purposes: some provide context, some receive notifications, and others allow an agent to write or send information.

title: Connect your revenue stack · Map connections to the workflow
text: CRM Account, contact, opportunity and field context Read/write scope, object coverage and record ownership Calendar Meeting identification and scheduling context Connected calendars, organizer identity and attendee visibility Meeting platform or recorder Recordings and transcripts Recording mode, consent and access to historical recordings Email Conversation context and drafts or sending Mailbox identity, delegated access and send approval Slack or Teams Briefs, alerts and collaboration Channel or user destinations and app permissions Usage/support sources Customer-health and expansion context Available events, account association and sync cadence

title: Connect your revenue stack · Before connecting
text: Confirm that the installing user has the required organization permissions. A personal account connection and an organization-level administrative integration can expose different data. Select the smallest scope that satisfies the workflow. Confirm the exact connector documentation and approved installation link for the current environment. The Help Center includes older web.oliv.ai routes; the current marketing navigation also uses my.oliv.ai. This V1 does not redirect users into an assumed login or installation flow.

title: Connect your revenue stack · Verify the connection
text: After installation, check a known record or meeting. Confirm that source ownership, timestamps and associations appear as expected, then test the downstream task. A logo or listed vendor is not evidence that a connector is installed or authorized for that workspace. Record how to revoke the connection and what happens to already imported data. If removal requires Oliv support, make that dependency explicit in the runbook.

title: Run a first workflow
text: Begin with a low-volume, identifiable case so the team can explain exactly what happened and why.

title: Run a first workflow · Choose a representative case
text: Select a meeting linked to an active opportunity, a CRM field update with clear evidence, or an account review with known risk signals. Avoid starting with a broad historical cleanup or a large outbound audience. Identify the expected source data and the person responsible for checking the result. Remove ambiguity about who owns an opportunity or which account a conversation concerns before judging the agent output.

title: Run a first workflow · Recommended first-run sequence
text: Confirm that the selected agent or workflow is enabled for the workspace. Check the source connections and the relevant account or opportunity. Review the applicable process rules and configured action permissions. Trigger the workflow using the verified production mechanism. Inspect the output, source evidence, destination and any approval request. Accept or reject the result through the verified interface and check the resulting state.

title: Run a first workflow · Do not use the prototype as an execution guide
text: The supplied October 15 extraction describes a frontend prototype. It records controls whose actions or persistence were not implemented in that source. Labels such as Run Agent, Clone Agent or Send therefore cannot establish the production procedure. The current V1 describes the intended workflow and verification requirements. Exact production clicks, error messages and expected save states must be confirmed in a running environment before this page becomes an end-user tutorial.

title: Who uses Oliv · Separate persona, role and entitlement
text: A page saying an agent is useful for a manager does not prove that only managers can run it. Likewise, a seat group such as Sell or Grow is a commercial grouping, not a verified RBAC role. For each action, establish who may see source data, configure agents, approve work, write to external systems and administer connections. Use the access reference for the questions that still need an owner decision.

title: Startups and staged adoption
text: The current startup presentation combines app access, connected context and selected agent work. A smaller team can still benefit from a carefully bounded first workflow.

title: Startups and staged adoption · Choose the initial scope
text: Start with the activity sources the team actually uses and the workflow that creates the clearest operational value. Examples include meeting preparation, reviewed CRM updates or a recurring pipeline review. A low seat fee is not the entire cost of operation. Identify agent usage, selected add-ons, implementation work and any hardware or external-service dependency before comparing total cost.

title: Startups and staged adoption · Recommended staged deployment
text: Connect the minimum source set for the first task. Agree the current ICP, ownership and qualification rules. Use reviewed outputs while the team verifies the workflow. Measure actual usage and the quality of the handoff. Expand to another team or job only after the first scope is dependable.

title: Startups and staged adoption · Commercial conditions
text: The website’s startup framing and sample cost comparisons are not a signed quote or proof of a universal discount. Use the current role-group pricing as a dated reference and obtain the offer applicable to the team. Keep current capabilities separate from custom agents or integrations that still require implementation.

Buyer, ICP and evaluation guides
text: Understand ideal-fit signals, the buying committee, company-stage scenarios and the complete 735-question buyer universe.

title: Buyer, ICP and evaluation guides · Practical fit signals
text: A B2B revenue motion with recurring customer interactions and identifiable account or opportunity ownership. An existing CRM and an accountable owner for revenue definitions and field mappings. Permitted access to representative interaction data and a team willing to review AI proposals. A specific sales or post-sale workflow with a measurable baseline and named sponsor.

title: Buyer, ICP and evaluation guides · Qualify the deployment before purchase
text: The supplied ICP materials contain several segmentation models, and the current website also has a startup offer. Treat rep, employee and ARR bands as planning context, not universal eligibility rules. Confirm actual supported segments, minimum commitments and deployment prerequisites with Oliv.

title: Buyer, ICP and evaluation guides · Fit concerns to resolve
text: An expectation that Oliv replaces the CRM conflicts with the approved complement positioning. No accountable CRM or revenue-process owner makes mapping and governance difficult. No lawful access to interactions or no review owner prevents a credible pilot. A requirement for a native category such as full CLM, LMS, ICM or reverse ETL needs explicit product evidence.

title: Buyer, ICP and evaluation guides · Firmographic and market context
text: The supplied ICP research emphasizes B2B revenue organizations, especially SaaS and IT services, with multiple customer interactions and a need for consistent execution. It also discusses financial services, logistics, healthcare and other verticals as research segments. Inclusion here does not establish industry-specific compliance or implementation support. The research discusses US-led buying alongside EMEA and APAC teams and remote or hybrid work. Confirm supported regions, recording rules, languages, data residency and communication channels for the actual deployment.

title: Buyer, ICP and evaluation guides · Technographic readiness
text: CRM Account, contact, opportunity and field ownership Supported connector, objects, schemas and write permissions Meeting and recording stack Source interaction evidence Organizer eligibility, capture mode, consent and recording rights Calendar and email Meeting identity and between-meeting context User identity, read scopes, sending scopes and tenant restrictions Chat and notification channels Daily review and ownership Recipient scope, permissions, escalation and supported actions Engagement, dialer or CS systems Additional activity and account signals Named product, supported artifacts, freshness and licensing Process definitions Methodology and approval consistency Accountable handbook owner, current definitions and change approval

title: Buyer, ICP and evaluation guides · Behavioral readiness signals
text: Leadership has chosen a specific AI workflow and accepts human review while behavior is validated. A process owner can resolve conflicting definitions rather than asking an agent to infer company policy. Managers and reps will inspect evidence and correct proposals instead of accepting every generated answer. The team can provide a representative pilot cohort and compare results with its current operating baseline.

title: Buyer, ICP and evaluation guides · Buying triggers and the first decision
Buyer, ICP and evaluation guides · Repeated forecast misses
text: Reconcile past submissions and actuals. Determine whether the issue is stale CRM data, inconsistent definitions, missing deal evidence or judgment. Evaluate Forecaster against that diagnosed problem rather than a universal accuracy promise.

title: Buyer, ICP and evaluation guides · CRM hygiene and administration
text: Identify unreliable fields and activities and their owners. Test proposed updates, rejected suggestions and CRM validation rules before widening write access.

title: Buyer, ICP and evaluation guides · Existing vendor renewal
text: Evaluate actual workflow value and total cost. Compare current quotes and requirements; historical competitor prices in the master are not purchasing evidence.

title: Buyer, ICP and evaluation guides · Team growth and process inconsistency
text: Document stages, ownership, qualification and handoffs before expanding. Test that multiple managers and teams interpret the same process consistently.

title: Buyer, ICP and evaluation guides · Uneven rep development
text: Agree the skill or behavior to improve, a reviewed scorecard and manager involvement. Inspect call examples and progress rather than assuming a score causes higher win rates.

title: Buyer, ICP and evaluation guides · Renewal risk and missed expansion
text: Reconcile renewal data and account ownership. Review risk and growth signals with CS and sales before creating opportunities or customer messages.

title: Buyer, ICP and evaluation guides · Leadership AI initiative or build-versus-buy review
text: Bound the required workflow, data and controls. Compare maintenance and governance effort for the actual options; the master’s content plans are not measured product comparisons.

title: Buyer, ICP and evaluation guides · Qualification questions
text: What recurring revenue workflow creates the greatest measurable operating burden? Which CRM and source systems own the necessary records and interactions? Who can authorize access, define the process and review outputs? Which approval, security, legal and procurement requirements are non-negotiable? Which result and exception case would prove this workflow useful? Which required capability lacks evidence in the evaluation map? What is the approved seat, credit, implementation and renewal cost for this deployment?

title: Agent configuration
text: Configuration determines what an agent may know, what starts its work and what actions it may take. The available sources describe several controls but do not establish every production rule.

title: Agent configuration · Configuration areas
text: Instructions and process The job and applicable rules Process Graph and agent reference Tools and approvals Available actions and review requirements Action boundaries Triggers and schedules Events or cadences that initiate work Triggers and schedules Knowledge and data Supporting documents and source access Knowledge and data Run history Evidence of attempted and completed work Run history

title: Agent configuration · Prototype versus production
text: The October extraction describes a prototype where several selections exist only for the visit and some action buttons have no implementation. That is useful UI evidence, but it cannot establish persistence, permission enforcement or a working execution path. Use these references to define what must be checked in the current workspace. Do not promote a selector option into a production guarantee merely because it is visible in the prototype.

title: Tool modes and action boundaries
text: Approval terminology differs across the sources. Establish the rule for each action rather than assuming one setting governs every workflow.

title: Tool modes and action boundaries · Labels in the sources
text: Prototype tool selector Auto Run; Requires Approval; Agent Decides Observed UI options; runtime enforcement unverified Prototype super-agent conversation Ask before acting; Act without asking Separate conversation control; precedence unverified CRM Manager source Ask First; Auto-Pilot Described CRM review/automatic modes Oliver source Human sign-off for handbook changes Described process-governance boundary Prospector live page Rep reviews first email; follow-ups can be automatic Specific outbound behavior to confirm in deployment

title: Tool modes and action boundaries · Precedence is unresolved
text: The prototype does not define which setting wins if a conversation control and a tool mode disagree. It also does not demonstrate an approval queue. This does not prove the live product lacks those features. Before writing an end-user procedure, confirm scope, default, persistence and enforcement for each setting. Check whether an administrator can restrict it and whether a user can override it.

title: Tool modes and action boundaries · Recommended approval contract
text: State the exact action being approved and the destination system. Show the proposed record values or complete outbound content. Identify the reviewer and expiry or escalation rule. Define reject, edit, cancel and retry behavior. Record the result and the identity used for the external action. Specify what happens if the underlying record changes while approval is pending.

title: Tool modes and action boundaries · Recommended checks
text: Test a read-only task, a draft, a CRM update and a customer-facing message separately. Verify that an unapproved action does not execute and that a rejected item remains understandable. The prototype’s Auto Run display default is not proof that agents execute without approval in production. That claim remains blocked until observed or explicitly confirmed by the implementation owner.

title: Triggers and schedules
text: An agent may start from a request, a source event or a schedule. The trigger mechanism and the action permission are separate decisions.

title: Triggers and schedules · Trigger types described in sources
text: Activity-driven New meeting, call or email context Supported event and completion condition Record change Opportunity or account state changes Fields, filters and event ordering Scheduled Forecast and portfolio review cadence Timezone, recurrence and delivery Direct request Ask an agent to prepare or analyze work User identity and permitted scope

title: Triggers and schedules · Schedule rules to document
text: Record the timezone, recurrence, owner, effective start and destination. State how holidays, missed runs, daylight-saving changes and unavailable inputs are handled. The prototype schedule dialog contains fixed timezone text and does not demonstrate persistence. Its displayed timezone is not a workspace policy, and a closed dialog does not prove a schedule was created.

title: Triggers and schedules · Stop and duplicate conditions
text: For event-driven work, confirm duplicate suppression, concurrent runs and what happens when a source record changes again. For customer outreach, confirm reply, opt-out, ownership change and manual-pause behavior. The available sources do not establish a universal agent pause, global stop or automatic undo facility. Those must be verified before they appear as product instructions.

title: Triggers and schedules · Recommended trigger acceptance test
text: Create a known qualifying event in a controlled scope. Verify one corresponding run and its input record. Repeat or modify the event and observe duplicate handling. Check a non-qualifying event that should not start work. Pause or disable the verified trigger path and confirm the observed result.

title: Knowledge and data access
text: An agent’s context can include organization process knowledge, source records and task-specific supporting material. Uploading a file and authorizing a connector are different operations.

title: Knowledge and data access · Types of context
text: Organization playbook Approved operating rules, methodology and exceptions Task-specific knowledge Relevant supporting material for a particular job Connected records Accounts, contacts, opportunities and activity Conversation evidence Recordings, transcripts, email and messages within authorized scope

title: Knowledge and data access · Source and access controls
text: Confirm who may add, replace or remove knowledge, whether access follows the source system, and whether individual or team information can be exposed to other users. The prototype lists import sources and accepted upload formats, but several import actions have no working behavior. A named source is not a confirmed connector; a prototype file-count label is not a commercial storage limit.

title: Knowledge and data access · Lifecycle and updates
text: Document when changed knowledge becomes available to an agent, how obsolete content is replaced, what is retained after removal and whether historical outputs continue to cite the prior version. Treat source provenance as part of the workflow. A current rule and an obsolete document can both be retrievable; the product owner must establish how conflicting or superseded material is handled.

title: Knowledge and data access · Recommended verification
text: Use a controlled document with a distinct fact, update that fact, and check subsequent answers and actions. Remove access and verify that the relevant user and agent cannot continue to retrieve restricted content. Do not claim organization-wide knowledge isolation, automatic deletion from every derived store or a fixed refresh SLA from the current materials.

title: Run history and outputs
text: Run history should help a user explain what an agent attempted, what it produced and what happened next.

title: Run history and outputs · Run concepts
text: Trigger Why work began Input context The record and source information used Attempt A particular execution of the job Output The prepared answer, draft, proposed change or completed action Review state Whether a human decision is required or recorded Destination result What the receiving system accepted or rejected

title: Run history and outputs · What the prototype establishes
text: The extraction records run lists, a details drawer, output presentations and an Agent Feed. Its runs are hand-written examples, predominantly successful, rather than production telemetry. Those examples do not establish complete logging of every action, failure-state coverage, retention, pagination, export or an audit guarantee. A cleared feed row is also not evidence that a run or its source data was deleted.

title: Run history and outputs · Recommended evidence for a support case
text: Agent and workflow name. Time, timezone and initiating event. Account, opportunity or meeting identifier. Observed output and destination. Approval or rejection state if shown. Error text or the point where expected behavior stopped.

title: Run history and outputs · Rules to verify
text: Confirm failed, queued, running, cancelled and retried states; whether retries create new attempts; what the user can correct; and how long history is retained. If native run IDs or logs are unavailable, describe the support process that actually exists. Do not invent a run export API or a retry button.

title: Platform concepts
text: Oliv’s platform story is a sequence from customer activity to connected context and useful action, with process knowledge guiding how agents operate.

title: Platform concepts · A conceptual model
text: Capture brings in the activity. Context Graph associates it with business entities. Signal Graph interprets revenue questions. Process Graph supplies the organization’s rules and exceptions. Agents prepare or execute work using that context; apps organize the related team workflows. This is a user-level explanation of the current product presentation. It is not a backend deployment diagram, a database schema or a guarantee about internal event ordering.

title: Platform concepts · Keep the concepts distinct
text: An activity is an input; a signal is an interpretation of that input; a process rule defines how the organization should act; an agent performs a job; an app is a workspace for related work. Keeping those terms separate makes it easier to explain an incorrect result and identify its owner.

title: Context Capture
text: Context Capture brings customer activity into Oliv so teams and agents can work from more than manually entered CRM notes.

title: Context Capture · Activity sources
text: The current website describes meetings, phone calls, email, messages and in-person conversations, alongside connected business records and supporting data. Availability depends on the source, integration, plan and organization configuration. For each source, distinguish metadata from full content. An event title or call log is not a transcript; a linked email is not necessarily a mailbox-wide archive. Confirm the actual imported fields, access scope and historical coverage. Online meetings Organizer, recording mode, consent, transcript and participant access Phone calls Supported dialer or capture route and recording availability Email Mailbox scope, included threads, attachments and retention Messaging Connected workspace/channel scope and supported history In-person activity Supported capture application/device and upload process CRM and usage/support data Objects, fields, event coverage and sync direction

title: Context Capture · Recording has conditions
text: The May 2026 recording guide distinguishes internally organized meetings from externally organized meetings when native recording is enabled. An external organizer can require a visible note taker and lobby admission. A claim that Oliv supports botless recording should therefore include the platform and organization prerequisites. Do not describe every meeting as botless or assume the same behavior for every conferencing tool.

title: Context Capture · Recommended verification
text: Before relying on a downstream agent, check a known activity for its content, participants, timestamps and destination record. Check what happens to private, cancelled, declined or inaccessible meetings, and how a user stops capture. Missing context can cause an incomplete result without indicating a reasoning failure. Troubleshooting should first establish whether the source activity arrived and was accessible.

title: Context Graph
text: Context Graph is the relationship layer that places customer activity against the business entities it concerns.

title: Context Graph · What the graph connects
text: The public product description associates conversations and activities with accounts, contacts and opportunities, using relationship history and conversation context rather than only an email-domain match. A useful activity association should preserve a path back to its source. Review the account, the particular opportunity and the participants before allowing an agent’s interpretation to affect a customer record.

title: Context Graph · Cases that need careful review
text: Several open opportunities at one company The activity belongs to the right product, motion and buying group A partner call mentions several customer accounts Each discussed customer is associated appropriately An acquisition changes the email domain The relationship to the prior entity remains understandable Duplicate or stale CRM accounts The active record is identified without unsafe merging Several deals discussed in one meeting Shared activity does not overwrite unrelated opportunity state

title: Context Graph · Association and CRM cleanup are separate decisions
text: Choosing the likely opportunity for an activity is not the same as authorizing a destructive CRM merge. The CRM Manager document explicitly leaves duplicate-resolution thresholds unresolved. Verify the current review and correction path for an incorrect association. This V1 does not claim a confidence threshold, automatic merge policy or guaranteed perfect mapping.

title: Context Graph · Recommended acceptance criteria
text: Use examples of multiple opportunities, duplicates and changed domains in the first deployment review. Require an explanation of the selected record, source evidence and a way to correct an incorrect association. Document whether a correction changes only the current activity or also related historical associations. That behavior is not established by the available sources.

title: Signal Graph
text: Signal Graph describes Oliv’s interpretation layer: activity is turned into revenue-relevant context that can be updated as new evidence arrives.

title: Signal Graph · What a signal means
text: A signal can represent an observed risk, qualification detail, stakeholder change, customer need or expansion indication. It is an interpretation grounded in source activity, not an independently guaranteed outcome. The website presents specialized models for revenue questions. This V1 explains the user-facing behavior without treating model counts or accuracy claims as verified benchmarks.

title: Signal Graph · Read the signal with its evidence
text: Identify the question the signal is answering. Check the account or opportunity and the source activity. Distinguish a directly stated fact from an interpretation or recommendation. Check whether newer information changed the signal. Confirm how the signal reaches the relevant agent or workflow.

title: Signal Graph · Illustrative workflow
text: An account conversation indicates that a previously supportive stakeholder has changed roles. The account association gives the signal a business location; the process playbook supplies the escalation rule; an agent can prepare a recommended next step. This example explains the relationship between concepts. It is not a promise that a specific trigger, threshold or escalation is enabled in every workspace.

title: Signal Graph · Rules still requiring confirmation
text: Confidence display, refresh timing, human corrections, conflicting evidence and downstream recalculation need production verification. The documentation should describe those rules once established rather than substituting a generic ‘AI confidence’ explanation. For forecast and health workflows, evaluate the signal against observed outcomes over time. A product example or forecast percentage on a marketing page is not a performance commitment.

title: Process Graph
text: Process Graph supplies company-specific operating context so agents can apply the team’s actual standards rather than generic sales advice.

title: Process Graph · What belongs in the playbook
text: The product presentation includes linked knowledge about the market, personas, prospecting, qualification, sales execution, handoffs, onboarding and customer success. The Oliver document adds ownership, methodology, approvals, territory rules and exceptions. State how the organization currently operates. If a process is aspirational or only proposed, mark that state explicitly. An unapproved process should not silently become the operating rule for customer communications or CRM changes.

title: Process Graph · How process changes are maintained
text: Oliver’s source documentation describes translating leader and RevOps input into structured handbook updates and aligning dependent agents. It also describes proposing learned changes for human sign-off. The exact approval interface, authorized approver, propagation timing, version history and rollback behavior are not established for all deployments. Those are governance requirements to confirm before allowing broad process changes.

title: Process Graph · Illustrative rule
text: A qualification rule can specify what evidence is required before an opportunity advances. An exception can state who may approve advancement when a required stakeholder is unavailable. A useful documentation entry includes the rule, scope, owner, effective date, evidence and exception path. This is a recommended rule format, not a claim that every field is currently configurable in Oliv.

title: Process Graph · Handle conflicting process sources
text: When two documents disagree on authority or a threshold, retain the conflict and ask the accountable owner to resolve it. Recency alone is not a reason to override an approved policy. Use the same approved process vocabulary across agent references, integration mappings and task guides. That prevents a renamed stage or qualification field from receiving several inconsistent explanations.

title: Agent execution and coordination
text: The agent layer combines a defined job, relevant context, available tools and an action boundary. Coordination determines which specialist handles the work.

title: Agent execution and coordination · The parts of an agent workflow
text: Job and instructions Define the intended work and success condition Context Provide the relevant account, opportunity and process knowledge Tools Read or change information through supported connections Trigger or request Start work from a verified event, schedule or user interaction Review boundary Determine what needs human confirmation Run result Show the output, destination and any unresolved issue

title: Agent execution and coordination · Super agents and specialists
text: Olivia is presented as the frontline execution and orchestration agent. Oliver maintains the process and configuration context. Specialist agents focus on particular jobs such as forecast preparation, CRM updates or coaching. The current public pages provide this conceptual distinction. The prototype’s dropdowns and demo run data do not establish production permission enforcement or runtime precedence.

title: Agent execution and coordination · Confirm boundaries per action
text: Separate read-only analysis, draft creation, CRM writes, outbound sending and process configuration. One general ‘autonomous’ label is insufficient to explain those different consequences. For each action, document whose identity is used, who can enable it, whether approval expires, where the request appears, what is logged and how a failed or rejected action is handled. These are acceptance questions until verified.

title: Apps
text: Apps group related team workflows. Agents perform jobs that can contribute to those workflows; the app name and the agent name are not interchangeable.

title: Apps · App and agent relationship
text: Converse Conversation capture, library and activity context Meeting Assistant, Researcher and CRM Manager Forecast Opportunity management and forecasting Forecaster, Deal Driver and CRM Manager Engage Prioritization and outreach execution Prospector and reactivation workflows Enable Coaching and useful conversation examples Coach and Content Curator Retain Customer health and account management Portfolio Manager and Gold Digger

title: Apps · Commercial grouping
text: The current pricing page uses role-based groups called Amplify, Converse, Sell and Grow. Sell includes Converse and Forecast; Grow includes Sell and Retain. Engage and Enable are presented as separately priced additions. That summary is a dated website description. Exact entitlements, usage costs and any negotiated agreement must be confirmed for the workspace.

title: Converse app
text: Converse is the conversation-capture workspace: bring recordings, transcripts and related activity into a searchable source of customer context.

title: Converse app · Capture sources
text: The current app page presents online meetings, phone and in-person capture alongside connected email and messages. Each channel depends on its supported integration and configuration. For online meetings, distinguish native/botless recording from a visible note taker. A platform-level capture claim does not mean every meeting uses the same recording route.

title: Converse app · Conversation library and context
text: The app provides a place to find and review conversations and useful moments. Source activity can support meeting preparation, CRM updates, coaching and account-level understanding. Searchability and downstream use depend on access to the original recording or transcript. Confirm which users can view, share or export each item and how source permissions are preserved.

title: Converse app · Recording prerequisites
text: Confirm the connected calendar, meeting platform, organizer, organization recording setup and consent or recording indication. If a visible note taker must enter a lobby, it may need admission before recording can begin.

title: Converse app · Limits and verification
text: Storage, retention, upload formats, recording duration, transcription languages and processing times need current plan-specific evidence. The website’s advertised language count does not establish accuracy for every language or accent. The app’s capture scope is separate from the permissions of agents that use the resulting context. Verify both before a wider rollout.

title: Forecast app
text: Forecast organizes opportunity and pipeline work, including forecast boards, submissions, snapshots and deal context.

title: Forecast app · Opportunity workspace
text: The current product presentation includes opportunity grids, qualification tracking, buying-committee context, deal risk, forecast boards, submissions, snapshots and change history. A grid view, a forecast category and a submitted forecast are separate concepts. Define the current view and the source of each field before comparing two numbers.

title: Forecast app · Forecast operating cadence
text: Forecaster’s internal reference describes contributor preparation, manager review and an admin/observer configuration layer. Targets, measurements and cadence determine how the process is organized. Document the actual hierarchy and rollup rule for the workspace. Multi-level approvals, custom formulas and automated mode transitions remain owner-confirmation items.

title: Forecast app · Snapshots and change history
text: A snapshot preserves a historical view used for comparison; a submission records the forecast entered for a cycle; deal change history tracks movement in individual records. They should not be described as one feature. Confirm snapshot frequency, retention and whether corrected source data changes historical views. The prototype includes multiple deal surfaces and does not establish which is the current production grid.

title: Forecast app · Boundaries
text: Do not publish a fixed forecast-accuracy percentage or a guaranteed progression to autonomous operation from the available examples. Check results against the workspace’s actual history and sales motion.

title: Engage app
text: Engage is the workspace for account prioritization and outreach, using shared account context to organize the next action.

title: Engage app · Engagement work
text: The live page describes a ranked account queue, contextual next actions, email and LinkedIn workflows, plays, signals and flows, with optional calling or messaging channels. A prioritized account is an input to a workflow. It does not by itself authorize sending or establish that a contact is eligible for outreach.

title: Engage app · Agents in the workflow
text: Prospector prepares account prioritization and outreach. The public page also presents a reactivation workflow for stalled accounts. The exact current agent identity, stop conditions and supported sequence behavior require confirmation. The Prospector page distinguishes a human-reviewed first email from automatic no-response follow-ups. Treat that as a specific described policy to verify, rather than assuming every channel has the same rule.

title: Engage app · Channel configuration
text: Confirm the primary mailbox, additional mailboxes, phone number and calling allowance, and each selected messaging channel. Sending identity, ownership, stop conditions and external platform limits belong in the setup contract. The current sources do not establish a universal rate limit, bounce threshold or opt-out implementation. Those require the current connector and sending-policy documentation.

title: Engage app · Current pricing conflict
text: The live Engage page shows a $39 starting figure in some sections and $29 in another. The main pricing page describes a $29 per-user monthly add-on to an app subscription. This V1 preserves the conflict for commercial review and does not turn either page into a contractual quote. Use the approved order form and current commercial owner’s confirmation.

title: Enable app
text: Enable groups coaching and enablement work: identify useful development goals and make strong conversation examples reusable.

title: Enable app · The enablement loop
text: Coach supplies scoring, recommended focus areas and progress tracking. Content Curator supplies relevant examples from accessible recordings. Managers and enablement owners use those outputs to support development. The current team page presents a multi-stage enablement process. This V1 describes the documented job relationship rather than claiming every illustrated tab or control is available.

title: Enable app · Scorecards and goals
text: The internal material describes configurable scorecards and criteria, manager-reviewed monthly goals and weekly progress. Confirm the current scorecard library, weighting and supported team scope. A call score is not a formal performance decision. Establish who can see the evidence and how a manager can correct a recommendation before using the workflow in a personnel process.

title: Enable app · Clips and access
text: Define the intent for useful examples, the library destination and the people who may view or share the clip. A clip should preserve the link and context needed to understand the source conversation. Historical backfill, external LMS syncing and detailed storage limits remain unresolved in the source material.

title: Enable app · Packaging
text: Enable appears on the current pricing page as an add-on. A team’s enablement use case does not establish entitlement for every user; verify seats, credit costs and the selected package before rollout.

title: Retain app
text: Retain groups account-health and customer-management workflows around conversations, account context and renewal priorities.

title: Retain app · Account workspace
text: The current pricing presentation associates Retain with customer grids, health scorecards, churn risks, retention forecasting, product usage, support context, whitespace and stakeholder tracking. These are capability categories. Verify the current integrations and data coverage before describing a specific usage event, support system or health formula.

title: Retain app · Review and intervention
text: Portfolio Manager prepares account and portfolio priorities with contributing evidence. The team decides the intervention, owner and due date. Gold Digger handles the distinct expansion-signal and warm-handoff motion. A renewal risk score is an interpretation; a renewal forecast is a projection; a customer-facing action is another step. Explain the states separately in operational documentation.

title: Retain app · Prerequisites
text: Confirm account ownership, renewal dates, health standards, the conversation sources and any usage or support connection. Identify which people may see individual accounts and full portfolio views. Where a data feed is missing, state the resulting coverage limitation. Do not infer usage decline or support risk from an unavailable source.

title: Retain app · Boundaries
text: The available documentation does not establish a complete support-ticketing replacement, a universal churn prediction accuracy or every account-management automation. Resolve current CS agent names before publishing a broader roster.

title: Workflows
text: A workflow reference explains the intended outcome and the boundaries between steps. Exact production controls are included only when supported by current evidence.

title: Workflows · The workflow evidence standard
text: Each operational guide should identify prerequisites, trigger, steps, result, alternate paths, errors and permissions. A source-backed concept can be drafted before a current click path is confirmed, but it must not pretend an untested control works. The recommended acceptance checks in this V1 are editorial test plans. They are distinct from documented product behavior.

title: Prepare and follow up a meeting
text: Use account, stakeholder and opportunity context to prepare for a conversation and turn it into reviewed follow-through.

title: Prepare and follow up a meeting · Before you start
text: A supported calendar connection and the relevant meeting. Correct participant and account/opportunity association. Access to prior context and the active qualification framework. A recording or transcript for post-meeting outputs.

title: Prepare and follow up a meeting · Workflow sequence
text: This sequence describes the documented handoffs. Verify current production controls before using it as a click-by-click end-user procedure. Identify whether this is a first-contact meeting or an active-opportunity discussion. Use Researcher for first-contact background and Meeting Assistant for deal-aware preparation. Review the brief for participant roles, qualification gaps and a useful agenda. After the conversation is processed, review the proposed follow-up and field changes. Send or apply the result using the verified review path and check the destination.

title: Prepare and follow up a meeting · Expected result
text: The intended result is a useful brief before the meeting and a contextual draft, proposed updates and qualification flags afterward. The sources do not establish a single universal delivery time.

title: Prepare and follow up a meeting · Variations and exceptions
text: Multiple deals, changed participants, cancelled events and unavailable recordings can change the result. Confirm how the current environment selects the opportunity and when it reruns preparation.

title: Prepare and follow up a meeting · Recommended acceptance checks
text: The following checks are proposed validation work, not claims that the product already provides every control mentioned. Check a meeting with a known active opportunity. Check a first-contact meeting with no opportunity. Change a participant or time and observe refresh behavior. Confirm the approved brief timing and notification channel. Verify that an unsent draft remains distinct from a sent email.

Record meetings with Oliv
text: Understand when Oliv records natively and when a visible note taker joins, then check the prerequisites for your meeting.

title: Record meetings with Oliv · Before you start
text: The relevant calendar and meeting platform connection. Organization-level native recording setup where required. Appropriate platform permissions and recording indication. The ability to admit a visible note taker when needed.

title: Record meetings with Oliv · Workflow sequence
text: This sequence describes the documented handoffs. Verify current production controls before using it as a click-by-click end-user procedure. Identify who organized the meeting. If the organization has native recording enabled and an internal user organized it, check the supported native recording setup. If an external organizer owns the meeting, expect the visible note-taker route described by the current guide. Admit the note taker from the lobby where required and confirm that recording started. After processing, check the recording, transcript and meeting association.

title: Record meetings with Oliv · Expected result
text: The May 2026 guide describes native/botless recording for internally organized meetings and a visible note taker for externally organized meetings, conditional on organization setup.

title: Record meetings with Oliv · Variations and exceptions
text: Without native setup, an internal meeting is not automatically evidence of botless capture. Host permissions, lobby controls, platform settings and unsupported meeting conditions can prevent recording.

title: Record meetings with Oliv · Recommended acceptance checks
text: The following checks are proposed validation work, not claims that the product already provides every control mentioned. Verify the behavior for an internally organized test meeting. Verify an externally organized meeting with a lobby. Check the recording indication visible to participants. Confirm the stop or exclusion control for the current client. Check the resulting recording access and sharing boundary.

Review and apply CRM updates
text: Use a source conversation to understand a proposed record change, review it under the configured policy and verify the written result.

title: Review and apply CRM updates · Before you start
text: A supported CRM connection with the required object permissions. A known mapping for the target field. Correct activity-to-record association. A verified review or automatic-update policy.

title: Review and apply CRM updates · Workflow sequence
text: This sequence describes the documented handoffs. Verify current production controls before using it as a click-by-click end-user procedure. Open the relevant record and identify the source activity. Review the proposed value and the evidence behind it. Check the field type, destination object and whether newer human edits conflict. Approve, edit or reject through the actual supported review flow. Confirm the final value in the CRM and retain the available change evidence.

title: Review and apply CRM updates · Expected result
text: The intended result is a correctly associated, supported field or record update. A proposed value, a queued write and a CRM-accepted change are different states.

title: Review and apply CRM updates · Variations and exceptions
text: Expired authorization, read-only fields, validation rules, conflicting edits and ambiguous records can prevent a write. Do not solve these by broadening permissions or merging records without the responsible owner’s decision.

title: Review and apply CRM updates · Recommended acceptance checks
text: The following checks are proposed validation work, not claims that the product already provides every control mentioned. Test a standard field and a customer-specific mapped field. Reject one proposed change and confirm no write occurs. Compare the acting identity in the CRM with the agreed connector identity. Observe a validation failure and the actual retry/support behavior. Confirm the correction or recovery path for an incorrect update.

Run a pipeline review
text: Use Deal Driver’s prepared context to focus management time on deal changes, risk and decisions.

title: Run a pipeline review · Before you start
text: Current opportunity data and recent activity. Team ownership and the manager’s scope. Agreed risk criteria and review cadence. An understood destination for briefs and alerts.

title: Run a pipeline review · Workflow sequence
text: This sequence describes the documented handoffs. Verify current production controls before using it as a click-by-click end-user procedure. Review the prepared team or per-rep view for the chosen period. Identify changes and the evidence that makes a deal worth attention. Separate qualification gaps from timing, engagement or ownership issues. Decide the intervention and assign a responsible person. Check that follow-through is recorded in the supported workflow. Use Forecaster for the related forecast decision rather than treating every risk flag as a category change.

title: Run a pipeline review · Expected result
text: The intended output is a management review with prioritized decisions and attributable next steps, rather than another manual status collection.

title: Run a pipeline review · Variations and exceptions
text: Stale CRM fields or missing conversations can produce an incomplete view. Confirm source coverage before concluding that a deal is inactive or that a rep failed to act.

title: Run a pipeline review · Recommended acceptance checks
text: The following checks are proposed validation work, not claims that the product already provides every control mentioned. Compare a flagged deal with its latest activity. Check manager visibility across the intended team only. Confirm the date range and timezone of a summary. Verify the path from a suggested action to an owned next step.

Prepare and review a forecast
text: Move from opportunity evidence to contributor submission, manager review and a historical record of the forecast.

title: Prepare and review a forecast · Before you start
text: Configured categories, targets, measurements and cadence. Current opportunity values and ownership. A verified contributor/manager hierarchy. An agreed review and submission process.

title: Prepare and review a forecast · Workflow sequence
text: This sequence describes the documented handoffs. Verify current production controls before using it as a click-by-click end-user procedure. Check the board, period and measurement being forecast. Review proposed deal category, value or timing changes with their evidence. Accept, edit or reject recommendations using the supported controls. Submit the contributor forecast where the operating mode requires it. Review manager adjustments and the team rollup. Preserve the submission or snapshot used for later comparison.

title: Prepare and review a forecast · Expected result
text: A forecast should identify the period, measurement, submission state and review scope. The outcome is not established merely by displaying a recommended number.

title: Prepare and review a forecast · Variations and exceptions
text: Different periods, formulas, currency handling, stale records or incomplete rollup scope can explain a mismatch. Confirm those definitions before changing the forecast.

title: Prepare and review a forecast · Recommended acceptance checks
text: The following checks are proposed validation work, not claims that the product already provides every control mentioned. Reconcile a contributor number to the included opportunities. Check a manager adjustment separately from a rep submission. Verify snapshot cadence and whether historical values are preserved. Confirm the criteria for changing automation modes. Measure accuracy against actual outcomes using an agreed definition.

Run a coaching cycle
text: Turn scored work into a manager-selected goal, weekly progress and relevant conversation examples.

title: Run a coaching cycle · Before you start
text: Sufficient recorded work for the relevant motion. Configured scorecards and criteria. An authorized manager and participating rep. Access to evidence and example clips.

title: Run a coaching cycle · Workflow sequence
text: This sequence describes the documented handoffs. Verify current production controls before using it as a click-by-click end-user procedure. Review the available scoring and the evidence volume. Read the proposed focus areas in the monthly review. Choose, edit or replace the goal before it reaches the rep. Agree what progress against that goal means. Review weekly progress with supporting examples. Close the cycle and select the next development priority.

title: Run a coaching cycle · Expected result
text: The documented coaching loop combines analysis, a human goal decision and progress tracking. A scorecard alone is not the entire coaching process.

title: Run a coaching cycle · Variations and exceptions
text: Sparse or unrepresentative activity can produce weak patterns. The source leaves precise thresholds and some team scopes unresolved; confirm them before making performance judgments.

title: Run a coaching cycle · Recommended acceptance checks
text: The following checks are proposed validation work, not claims that the product already provides every control mentioned. Check the manager review step before goal delivery. Verify who can see the rep’s underlying activity. Correct a scoring error and observe later reporting. Confirm whether the workflow supports the chosen role and motion. Keep illustrative improvement percentages separate from measured results.

Review and hand off an expansion signal
text: Use Gold Digger’s evidence to confirm an expansion opportunity and prepare an owned, warm introduction.

title: Review and hand off an expansion signal · Before you start
text: Accessible customer conversations and account context. Known account and commercial ownership. The current customer footprint and relevant adjacent use cases. An approved handoff and communication policy.

title: Review and hand off an expansion signal · Workflow sequence
text: This sequence describes the documented handoffs. Verify current production controls before using it as a click-by-click end-user procedure. Review the detected signal and the original conversation moment. Check whether it represents an actual adjacent need or a routine comment. Confirm the stakeholder, account context and responsible commercial owner. Review the warm-introduction draft with the CSM or designated owner. Send or delegate through the approved route. Confirm the opportunity record and follow-through without creating duplicates.

title: Review and hand off an expansion signal · Expected result
text: The intended outcome is a reviewed signal with an owned next step. Detection, qualification, introduction and commercial conversion are different stages.

title: Review and hand off an expansion signal · Variations and exceptions
text: Conflicting account ownership, several expansion opportunities or a sensitive customer situation can change the handoff. The available sources do not establish a universal automatic qualification or sending policy.

title: Review and hand off an expansion signal · Recommended acceptance checks
text: The following checks are proposed validation work, not claims that the product already provides every control mentioned. Verify the source quotation and timestamp. Check the proposed stakeholder and existing opportunity records. Reject a signal and observe its resulting state. Confirm who reviews and who sends the introduction. Check the recorded opportunity’s source and ownership.

Review customer health and renewals
text: Use portfolio context to identify at-risk accounts, choose interventions and prepare CS management reviews.

title: Review customer health and renewals · Before you start
text: Account ownership and renewal dates. Current customer conversation and engagement context. Configured health criteria. Usage/support connections where the workflow depends on them.

title: Review customer health and renewals · Workflow sequence
text: This sequence describes the documented handoffs. Verify current production controls before using it as a click-by-click end-user procedure. Review the account or portfolio view for the selected period. Read the evidence behind a health or renewal-risk interpretation. Distinguish account risk from expansion potential and CSM coaching needs. Assign an intervention owner and a concrete next step. Prepare the manager or leadership review with the relevant account context. Check progress and update the supported record or task workflow.

title: Review customer health and renewals · Expected result
text: The intended result is a prioritized, evidence-bearing CS review. A color, score or projected renewal category is not a completed intervention.

title: Review customer health and renewals · Variations and exceptions
text: Missing usage feeds, outdated renewal data or unclear stakeholder ownership can weaken the view. A support ticket trend cannot be assumed when the support source is not connected.

title: Review customer health and renewals · Recommended acceptance checks
text: The following checks are proposed validation work, not claims that the product already provides every control mentioned. Compare a risk flag with current conversations and usage evidence. Check access to individual accounts versus portfolio totals. Confirm the definitions of renewal categories and health criteria. Verify how next actions are assigned and tracked. Resolve CS role and agent naming before exposing a broader roster.

Prepare an account outreach workflow
text: Review account priority and a point of view before starting an approved outreach motion.

title: Prepare an account outreach workflow · Before you start
text: The approved ICP and account territory. Account ownership and available first-party context. Configured channels and an authorized sending identity. Approved review, reply and stop conditions.

title: Prepare an account outreach workflow · Workflow sequence
text: This sequence describes the documented handoffs. Verify current production controls before using it as a click-by-click end-user procedure. Review why the account is prioritized now. Check the account context and proposed point of view. Review the opening communication before sending. Confirm the follow-up policy for the chosen channel. Observe replies, exclusions and ownership changes through the supported workflow.

title: Prepare an account outreach workflow · Expected result
text: The intended output is a contextual, reviewed start to outreach. Account ranking does not itself establish contact eligibility or a promise of conversion.

title: Prepare an account outreach workflow · Variations and exceptions
text: A reply through another channel, an ownership change or an excluded contact can affect subsequent actions. The current sources do not establish every sequence stop condition or cross-channel reconciliation rule.

title: Prepare an account outreach workflow · Recommended acceptance checks
text: The following checks are proposed validation work, not claims that the product already provides every control mentioned. Review the account and contact selection. Verify that the first message requires the described human decision. Test the configured reply and opt-out path before scaling. Confirm the actual volume, channel and credit limits. Keep preparation and sending permissions separate.

title: Integrations · Read support levels correctly
text: This V1 distinguishes a working setup described by a dated help article, a current marketed integration and a vendor named only in a picker or example. None of those establishes a fresh end-to-end test for your workspace. The current website’s broad integration count is not used as a connector-by-connector support matrix. Each connector still needs its own verified data and permission contract.

title: Integrations · Required connector contract
text: Authentication method and installing role. Read and write scopes, object types and field restrictions. Sync direction, cadence and source-of-truth rule. Historical import and refresh behavior. Rate limits, errors, retries and duplicate handling. Disconnect procedure and retained-data behavior. Plan, add-on and credit implications.

title: Salesforce integration · Data direction and permissions
text: The intended workflow reads CRM context and can write supported updates. The exact object, field and permission matrix is not available in the current sources.

title: Salesforce integration · Setup prerequisites
text: Obtain the current installation link and package version from the implementation owner. Confirm the installing role and organization policy; do not treat the older article’s package link or broad installation setting as a current default.

title: Salesforce integration · Disconnect and retained data
text: The dated guide directs removal requests through Oliv support. Verify the current disconnect procedure, token revocation and effect on retained data.

title: Salesforce integration · Connector contract to confirm
text: These are unresolved implementation questions. The list is not a claim that all of the named controls already exist. Which objects, custom objects and associations are supported? Which Salesforce identity performs each write? How do validation rules, duplicate rules and field-level security affect updates? How are conflicts with human edits resolved? What are the API consumption and retry rules? Which package and scopes are current?

title: Salesforce integration · Recommended connection check
text: Use a controlled source record or meeting, confirm that it arrives with the right owner and associations, and inspect any downstream write or notification. Repeat with a permission or validation exception and record the observed error path. Record the integration version, scopes, tested objects, plan and verification date. Keep that acceptance record current when the provider changes its API or permissions.
